question: What is the primary purpose of the WHO classification system for FGM?

options.A: To standardize clinical documentation and public health data
options.B: To determine the financial cost of surgical reconstruction
options.C: To legally prosecute traditional birth attendants in court
options.D: To prescribe specific herbal treatments for wound healing

explanation: Categorizing procedures helps health workers maintain consistent records and track prevalence accurately. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h1)

question: Why are non-medical procedures performed on female genitalia classified together as FGM?

options.A: They all lack therapeutic value and cause intentional physical harm
options.B: They share the exact same long-term psychological outcome
options.C: They always use identical surgical instruments and local anesthesia
options.D: They are exclusively performed by licensed medical doctors

explanation: Every type of FGM involves altering healthy female organs without medical necessity, causing physical and psychological damage. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h1)

question: Type Ia FGM specifically involves the removal of which anatomical structure?

options.D: The lower third of the vagina

explanation: Type Ia is defined strictly by the removal of the clitoral hood or prepuce without excising the body of the clitoris. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h2)

question: A patient presents with scarring and missing tissue limited strictly to the clitoris and its hood. Which FGM type is this?
explanation: Restricting the excision to the clitoris and prepuce falls under the Type I classification. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h2)

question: Which structure is removed in Type II FGM in addition to the clitoris?
explanation: Type II excision is characterized by the removal of the clitoris alongside the labia minora, with or without the labia majora. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h3)

question: A nursing assessment reveals a patient missing her clitoris and labia minora, with intact labia majora. What sub-type is this?
explanation: Removing both the clitoris and the labia minora without touching the labia majora matches the criteria for Type IIb excision. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h3)

question: What is another common medical term used for Type III FGM?
explanation: Infibulation is the specific term designated for the sealing procedure of Type III FGM. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h4)

question: Why must a tiny aperture be left intact during the infibulation procedure?

options.A: To prevent localized bacterial infections from forming
options.B: To permit normal unassisted vaginal childbirth
options.C: To allow the passage of urine and menstrual blood
options.D: To ensure future surgical access for routine pelvic exams

explanation: A small opening is strictly required for bodily waste fluids like urine and menses to exit the body. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h4)

question: Which procedure falls under the Type IV FGM category?

options.A: Radical removal of the clitoral body
options.B: Bilateral excision of the labia majora
options.C: Complete surgical sealing of the vaginal lips
options.D: Piercing or scraping of the genitalia

explanation: Type IV covers miscellaneous harmful acts like pricking, piercing, scraping, and cauterizing the genital organs. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h5)

question: How does Type IV FGM differ fundamentally from Types I, II, and III?

options.A: It includes non-excision injuries like pricking and cauterization
options.B: It is performed exclusively by certified gynecologists in hospitals
options.C: It never carries any risk of long-term infection
options.D: It is completely reversible without surgical intervention

explanation: Type IV acts as a catch-all for genital modifications that do not strictly involve removing tissue like the other three types. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h5)

question: Which of the following is an immediate complication of FGM?
explanation: Profuse bleeding happens immediately after tissue trauma and vascular injury during the cutting process. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h6)

question: A young woman who underwent Type III FGM presents in labor. Which complication is she most at risk for during delivery?

options.A: Premature closure of the fallopian tubes

explanation: The fibrotic scar tissue barrier impedes fetal descent, frequently leading to prolonged and obstructed labor. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h6)

question: What is an essential approach for community health nurses when addressing FGM in rural settings?

options.A: Reporting every community member to international criminal courts
options.B: Isolating families who practice tradition from receiving any healthcare
options.C: Focusing solely on surgical reversal without discussing prevention
options.D: Using culturally sensitive education and local stakeholder engagement

explanation: Lasting behavioral change requires respectful dialogue and collaboration with influential members within the local community. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h7)

question: Which duty is a primary clinical responsibility for a nurse caring for a survivor of FGM?

options.A: Diagnosing the exact traditional practitioner who cut the patient
options.B: Prescribing mandatory hormonal therapy for all patients
options.C: Providing empathetic support and managing physical complications
options.D: Performing immediate outpatient cosmetic genital reconstruction

explanation: Nurses focus on holistic care, treating physical ailments like infections and offering psychological comfort. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h7)
